staff.title: WHO RUNS THE GAME?
staff.directorText: Coordinates operations and staff. In tournaments, oversees structure, timing and organization; matters requiring a higher decision may be referred to the director under house procedures.
staff.floorText: Supervises tables and resolves questions, disputes and irregularities. Establishes what happened and applies house rules. If a problem arises, request the floor and preserve cards and chips until instructed.
staff.dealerText: Runs the hand: deals cards, tracks action order and manages bets and pots. Point out errors promptly; when interpretation or a dispute is involved, the dealer calls the floor.
decisions.title: POKER IS A GAME OF CONTINUOUS DECISIONS
decisions.intro: Every action or new card changes the situation. Pokerinno helps you go through the cycle again.
decisions.observeText: Your cards, position, pot and previous action: what do you know now?
decisions.optionsText: Fold, check, call, bet or raise? Check which actions are available and what each costs.
decisions.chooseText: Choose with a reason: seek value, control the pot, bluff or avoid further risk.
decisions.followText: Did an opponent respond or a new card appear? Update your assessment before the next choice.
decisions.reviewText: Understand your reasoning. Winning does not prove the choice was good; losing does not prove it was bad.
decisions.exampleText: On the flop, someone bets and action reaches you. What is the first step?
decisions.answerText: Observe before clicking. Compare the call amount with the pot, consider your potential to improve and what the opponent may represent. Calling keeps you in the hand but costs chips; folding avoids more spending but gives up the pot; raising invests more and changes the pressure. Without cards, stacks and full context, there is no single answer.

xp.rules: Editorial difficulty: true/false 10 XP; multiple choice 20 XP; ordering 30 XP; mathematics and showdown situations 40 XP. Every new correct response earns XP, including repeated activities. Review earns no points. Responses before this update remain in history without retroactive XP.
xp.dailyNote: Line for the last 14 days with recorded XP. Tap points to inspect values.
xp.empty: Your ranking starts with your next correct answer.

procedure.quantity: Correcting an incorrect number of cards also depends on being able to identify the cards reliably; the Floor determines the procedure.
procedure.flop: Other errors, such as a two-card flop or a flop opened before preflop action ends, also require a pause. Players do not choose which cards remain on the board or remove extra cards by agreement: the official procedure preserves randomness.
procedure.deck: A card from another deck or a foreign object also requires stopping to check deck integrity before continuing.
procedure.authority: House rules and the responsible official’s decision prevail; the dealer should not improvise an important correction.
procedure.summary: Shuffling, misdeals and irregularities: learn how to prepare cards and correct errors.
